title: Metabolic comorbidity in severe mental illness
bottleneck: People with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder die 10-20 years early, largely from cardiovascular and metabolic disease driven by both the illnesses and their treatments (antipsychotic-induced weight gain, diabetes). Psychiatry and primary care operate in silos, so metabolic risk goes unmanaged until crisis.
why_it_blocks: The mortality gap in severe mental illness is a public health emergency hiding inside psychiatry. Treating the mind while the body dies early is a partial medicine.
current_state: Metabolic monitoring guidelines exist but adherence is poor. GLP-1 agonists are being explored for antipsychotic-associated weight gain; integrated care models show promise but are rare. Metformin and GLP-1 agonists are being repurposed for antipsychotic-induced metabolic syndrome, but psychiatric and medical care remain organizationally siloed in most systems.
